fatal_errors: The proposed annealed, boron-doped HEA film system does not reconstruct the target comparison between thermally shocked bulk AlCoCrFeNi2.1 and duplex stainless steel 2205.
The NaCl film test omits the target's deionized-water temperature dependence and therefore cannot test the key nonmonotonic minimum in degradation near 50 °C.
Annealing and boron addition are changed simultaneously without anneal-only and boron-only controls, so their individual effects and any interaction cannot be identified.
The response does not separately predict or quantify the wear, corrosion, and synergistic components of combined degradation.
Self-healing is asserted but neither the cited evidence nor the proposed endpoint microscopy directly demonstrates repeated rupture and repassivation during sliding.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad HEA tribocorrosion problem and offers a scientifically plausible alternative centered on passive-film stability, repassivation, microstructural densification, and boride strengthening. Its proposed measurements could determine whether the combined treatment improves net OCP behavior, friction, and wear relative to an untreated film. However, it has little agreement with the hidden target: the alloy form, composition, comparator, thermal-shock protocol, aqueous medium, temperature/load/frequency matrix, lamellar L12/B2 mediator, and observed temperature-dependent wear regimes are all absent. The evidence is partially relevant but compositional: E1 supports annealing benefits in a different HEA film, while E2/E3 support boron-dependent wear and corrosion effects in another coating system. None directly establishes that combining annealing and boron creates a self-healing film under coupled tribocorrosion. A four-arm factorial design, time-resolved electrochemical recovery measurements, and explicit mechanical, corrosion, and synergy decomposition would make the alternative hypothesis substantially more discriminating.
